messages:
liam: Heads up — release gate for tonight's build is in the 23:00 UTC change window. Who's claiming the deployer for prod? We need a 5% canary pin and a clear rollback plan; also want to validate MFA/JIT for anyone who will press.

maria: I can claim if the window works for me. Quick Q: do we pin to commit sha or to the model version tag this time?

liam: Pin to commit sha (abcdef123). Keep canary at 5% for 30m. If error rate exceeds 3% or latency p90 > 350ms we roll back. @deploy-bot can you open a claim window?

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Deployer claim request registered for thread 2841239001. To accept run: `/claim deployer --thread 2841239001 --duration 60m`. Current claim: none. MFA_required: yes.

tia: FYI my YubiKey timed out last week during a push. If MFA is flaky for some people, what's fallback? We shouldn't use a SA for manual press unless emergency.

nora: Security policy: no long-lived SA for manual production deploys. If MFA/JIT fails, request temporary sudo via Okta JIT for identity `eng-releases` and tag your approval. I'll watch approvals. @sam if you think there's an emergency SA path, escalate to sec lead.

sam: I'll stand by. If JIT fails we can do a controlled canary-only rollout from CI without giving full deploy rights: `redwood deploy --pin=abcdef123 --canary=5 --monitor`

maria: Claiming now. Running `/claim deployer --accept`

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Deployer claimed by maria for 45m. Lock: MFA_required.

liam: Maria — checklist: 1) start 5% canary pinned to abcdef123 2) monitor the Redwood Console (errors, latency, cost) 3) post release notes link in this thread 4) if regressions -> rollback and note reason.

maria: On it. Release notes: https://notes.internal/releases/2026-03-20-v1.4.2

sam: Added a short healthcheck that hits /internal/health on canary instances; alert rule: error_rate > 3% or 5xx spikes.

tia: Oncall hooks set. Pager threshold mirrors what Sam set. If we need to rollback, what's the exact command?

sam: Rollback command (manual):
```
redwood rollback --to=previous --immediate --reason="canary regress"
```
If it's an automated rollback we have the auto-fallback in the route policy.

nora: Reminder: capture the Okta JIT approval in the audit log. I'll confirm the trace once the claim is active.

maria: Canary starting now :rocket:

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Canary rollout started for commit abcdef123 — 5% traffic. Canary window: 30m. Monitoring hooks: alert on error_rate > 3% or p90 latency > 350ms.

liam: Good. Keep updates short in this thread. If we need a rollback, call it immediately and ping #eng-sre.

maria: 23:10 UTC — quick update: error_rate 0.8%, p90 320ms. No alerts so far; continuing the canary.

tia: +1. No pager triggered.

maria: 23:26 UTC — canary looks stable. Proceeding to ramp to 100% over 10m.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Rollout progressing: 50% -> 100% over 10m.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Rollout complete to 100% for commit abcdef123. Release pinned to commit.

liam: Nice work — thanks everyone. Closing claim.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Deployer claim released by maria. Audit: JIT approval recorded.

maria: Added final note to release doc and flagged the metrics dashboard. :white_check_mark:
